questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹10,625 for 2 years at 8% interest per annum, if interest is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 10,625

Rate = 8%

Time = 2 years

Formula used:

A = P{1 + (r/100)t }

Where,

A = amount, P = principal, r = rate, t = time

Compound Interest = Amount – Principal

Calculation:

⇒ A = P × {1 + (r/100)t}

⇒ A = 10,625 × { 1 + (8/100)² }

⇒ A = 10,625 × (108/100)2

⇒ A = 10,625 × (1.08)²

⇒ A = Rs.12,393

Compound Interest = 12,393 –10,625 = Rs.1,768

∴ The compound interest for the given principal is Rs. 1,768.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Concept used:

The effective rate of R% for 2 years = R + R + R× Rover100

Calculation:

The effective rate of 8% for 2 years = 16.64%

⇒ 10625 × 16.64% = 1768

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1768.**

questions.question: Rs. 6000 is lent at the rate of 20 percent per annum on compound interest (compounded half yearly). What will be the compound interest of 18 months?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 6000

Rate = 20%

Time = 18 months

**Concept Used:**

A = P × (1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾

Where:

A = Amount

P = Principal

r = Annual interest rate 

n = Number of times the interest is compounded per year

t = Time period (in years)

**Calculation:**

The interest is compounded half-yearly, so n = 2 (twice a year).

The time period (t) is 18 months, which is equivalent to 1.5 years.

Rate, r = 20% = 0.20

Let's substitute these values into the formula:

A = 6000 × (1 + 0.20/2)⁽² × ¹.⁵⁾

⇒ 6000 × (1 + 0.10)³

⇒ 6000 × 1.10³

⇒ 6000 × 1.331

⇒ A = Rs. 7986

Compound interest = A - P

⇒ 7986 - 6000

⇒ Rs. 1986

Therefore, the compound interest for 18 months at a rate of 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly, would be Rs. 1986.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: At a certain sum of money with the interest rate of 6% per annum for 4 years. the simple interest is Rs. 4500. Find the compound interest (compounding annually) of 2 years at the same sum when the rate of interest is 4% per annum,
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate₁ = 6%

Time₁ = 4 years

Simple Interest = Rs. 4500

Time₂ = 2 years

Rate₂ = 4%

**Concept Used:**

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)T - P

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest = PRT/100

4500 = (P × 6 × 4)/100

P = (4500 × 100)/(6 × 4)

P = 750 × 25

P = Rs. 18750

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)T - P

Compound Interest = 18750(1 + 4/100)² - 18750

Compound Interest = 18750(26/25)2 - 18750

Compound Interest = 18750 × 676/625 - 18750 

Compound Interest = 20280 - 18750 

Compound Interest = 1530

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest (in Rs.) on a sum of Rs. 46,000 for 2(2)/(5) years at 15% per annum, interest being compounded annually (nearest to a Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Principal amount (P) = Rs. 46000

Rate (R) = 15%

Time (N) = 2(2)/(5) years

Concept used:

Compound interest, CI = P(1 + R/100)n - P

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

N = Time in years

Calculation:

The principal amount becomes

⇒ 46000 × (1 + 15/100)² = Rs. 60835

Now, for 2/5 years, the rate of interest becomes = 15% × 2/5 = 6%

Hence, the principal amount becomes

⇒ 60835 × (1 + 6/100)¹ = Rs. 64485.1

So, the interest accrued = 64485.1 - 46000 ≈ Rs. 18485

**∴ Rs. 18485 is the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 46,000 for 2(2)/(5) years at 15% per annum, interest being compounded annually.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

For the first two years, the rate of interest is 15%

Then, for the next 2/5 years, the rate of interest becomes

⇒ 15% × 2/5 = 6%

So, calculating the successive percentage of 15%, 15% and 6%, we get

⇒ {(15 + 15 + 6) + (15 × 15 + 15 × 6 + 15 × 6)/100 + (15 × 15 × 6)/(100 × 100)}%

⇒ 40.185%

So, the interest accrued = 46000 × 40.185% ≈ Rs. 18485

∴ Rs. 18485 is the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 46,000 for years at 15% per annum, interest being compounded annually.

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest on ₹6,400 for 1 year at 5% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.6400

Time = 1 year and rate = 5%

**Concept used:**

Compound interest (C.I) = P × Effective rate%

Effective rate% for 2 years = R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂)/100

**Calculation:**

For compounded annually:

C.I = 6400 × 5% = 320

For compounded half-yearly:

New rate = 5/2% = 2.5%

Time = 1 × 2 = 2 years

Effective rate% for 2 years = 2.5 + 2.5 + (2.5)²/100

⇒ 5 + 0.0625 = 5.0625%

C.I = 6400 × 5.0625% = Rs.324

Required difference = 324 - 320 = Rs.4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

questions.question: Radha deposited ₹1,60,000 at a 10% rate of compound interest per annum for two years. If the interest is compounded semi-annually, then what is the compound interest (in ₹)?

Rate (R) = 10%

**Concept used:**

Interest is calculated semi-annually (half-yearly) then

R = R/2 and T = 2T

**Formula used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + (R/100))T

Compound interest (CI) = A - P

**Calculation:**

Here interest is calculated half-yearly then,

⇒ R = 10/2 = 5% and T = 2 × 2 = 4 years

Now,

⇒ A = 160000 × (1 + (5/100))⁴

⇒ A = 160000 × (21/20)⁴

⇒ A = 194481

⇒ CI = 194481 - 160000 = 34481

**∴ The correct answer is Rs 34,481.**
